# dsh-session-bridge

Session-level multi-thread orchestration for DeepSeek Harness. Installs as a
bundle in a profile and

registers **globally** — every session can use the tools
regardless of agent preset.
## Tools
| Tool | Purpose |
| `session_create` | Create an ordinary session in the caller's workspace (optional initial prompt);
returns the session id. The child binds to the caller's standing composition via `composeFrom` — ne

ver re-mounts another preset. |
| `session_send` | Deliver a prompt to any ordinary session by id. `
queue` = next-turn FIFO (busy targets finish their turn first); `interrupt` = insert at the next ste
p boundary. Cold sessions resume automatically with their recorded preset mounted. Subagent sessions

are refused. |
| `session_list` | Enumerate ordinary sessions (id, title, cwd, running); optional w
`session_list` | Enumerate ordinary sessions (id, title, cwd, running); optional workspace filter. |

## Runtime compatibility

The plugin reads every service structurally through `ctx.get`, so one build
serves both DSH lines:

- **0.2.x (incl. DSH Desktop 0.2.0-rc.2)** — `sessionPersistence.list()` returns
detached snapshots

(`{ header, revision, sizeBytes }`); `session_list` and
cold-session `session_send` read `snapshot.h

eader`.
- **0.1.7-rc.1 and later 0.1.x** — the same listing returned bare
`SessionHeader` rows; the
normalization in `headerOf()` still accepts them.

Cold resume mounts `header.agentPreset` through `agentPresets.mount()` inside the
`setup` callback.

Without that, `agents.resume()` restores history but leaves the
agent without the preset's tools and

that, `agents.resume()` restores history but leaves the
agent without the preset's tools and prompt.
## Notes

- Send/creation use the harness's built-in session/agent services; the plugin
only wraps them into m

odel-facing tools.
- Cross-session messages are recorded with `source: { kind: 'session-bridge' }`.

DSH 0.2 removed the shared `kind: 'plugin'` source kind (each producer declares
its own), and every

consumer falls through an unknown kind to its generic
rendering.
- Only ordinary sessions are addres

sable; subagent-owned sessions keep the
subagent routing fence.
